hypothesis: Fault-tip halo dot placement: sparse predicted dots in the 100–300 m halo around fault tips and step-overs, where new-fault ground truth can exist within 300 m of a known trace (organizer forum thread 11516) while known-fault pixels themselves are masked from scoring. With alpha=0.2 < beta=0.8, missing truth costs more than a false positive, so placing mass in the scored, unmasked halo instead of on masked catalogue faults can outscore both a blank map and a catalogue-wasting map.
mechanism: Simulate a fault network of short disconnected line segments; dilate to a 1–3 px halo around fault cells; thin candidate halo pixels by inverse distance (closer to fault = higher kernel credit if new truth appears there); emit dots at 0.65 confidence. New faults nucleate as extensions of or step-overs between mapped traces — exactly the structure this rule targets.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Volcanic dike intrusion along a pre-existing lithospheric weakness that is not a slip-prone, seismogenic fault; the surface expression is a vent/fissure alignment rather than a scarp, so it would not be in the USGS/INGENIOUS scarp-based catalogue but could still align with the same structural corridor.
